status: NEW (Roman, 2026-09-20) — sibling law to fatelands_ordinary_wish_misalignment. That law governs what a wish's misfire may causally/visually look like; this law governs HOW a character may come to perceive that misalignment in the first place, so a scene can make misalignment legible through someone's words and observed response without inventing attack visuals.
cross_reference_note: CONSISTENT WITH, and formalizes for author/CG context, pre-existing project memory canon (project_fatelands_alignment_sense, Roman 2026-08-09/10, already wired into STARTER_SEEDS.starter_first_sacrifice worldTruths): ALL First Favored innately sense misalignment (a perceptual sense, like a sour note — NOT thoughts/emotions, NOT a light show — developed like a muscle by study and practice); Sacrificiants are First Favored whose sense has been specifically tuned/honed for this role; humans and Kwisheen lack the innate sense and rely on studied body-language reading. This law does not change that prior canon — it states it in the shared, Fatelands-wide, mechanically-consumable form the runtime directive stack and future packets need.

scope.applies_to: Fatelands Fantasy — any scene where a character's ability to notice/name/react to another person's misalignment (between stated words, ritual intent, and underlying desire) matters to the story.
explicitly_excluded: Famous Fate worlds (independently canonical, this law never applies)
scope.gate_contract: Runtime: _fatelandsFantasyWorldGate() in public/app.js — the same real gate every other Fatelands-conditional directive in this codebase uses.

statement.first_favored_innate_perception: First Favored possess an innate capacity to sense misalignment between a person's outward words, ritual intent, and underlying desire. Its acuity varies substantially by individual sensitivity and training. This is NOT telepathy, NOT certainty, and NOT a universal lie detector — it produces a PERCEPTION that must still be interpreted, and that perception can be mistaken.
statement.human_kwisheen_learned_perception: Humans and Kwisheen do not gain that innate sense, but can learn to recognize misalignment through study and practice: tells, microexpressions, body language, evasions, ritual habits, and contextual inconsistency. A trained observer's conclusion remains grounded_inference, not access to secret truth.
statement.weave_script_is_not_this: The First Favored's Weave-Script (the silver marking that glows/shifts with EMOTIONAL state) is a SEPARATE, unrelated bodily tell — it does NOT indicate misalignment and is not the mechanism of this perception. Misalignment is sensed, never read off Weave-Script color/glow. Conflating 'alignment sense' with 'Weave-Script' is a real, disclosed error this law corrects wherever it recurs (see _first_sacrifice_source_packet.json's corrected julian_strategic_logic_requirement).

hard_boundary: Never certainty. A character's perception (innate or learned) is always an interpretable reading, never proof, never mind-reading, never omniscience about another character's private thoughts or hidden wishes. It licenses a scene to make misalignment legible through recognition/naming/reaction — it never licenses inventing a specific fact about another character's private intent beyond what the scene's actual words/behavior support.
character_assignment_policy: This law states a GENERAL capability available to First Favored (innate) and to any trained human/Kwisheen observer (learned) — it does NOT itself assign sensitivity, training, or certainty to any specific character. Whether a given character has this capability, and how strong it is, must already be established by that story's own seed/canon (e.g. a character's established role, species, or training) before a beat cites this law as a named ground for that character's perception.

provenance_integration.valid_named_ground: grounded_inference may cite 'first_favored_alignment_sense' (innate) or 'trained_misalignment_observation' (learned) as a named ground — same schema slot as a facet, a relationship constraint, or an environment object (see claim_categories.grounded_inference) — ONLY when the citing character's capability is already independently established by that story's own canon. Citing this law does not itself establish the capability for an unestablished character.
provenance_integration.distinction_preserved: innate (first_favored_alignment_sense) and learned (trained_misalignment_observation) are DISTINCT named-ground values — a claim must specify which one applies and why (the character's species/role for innate; their study/practice/experience for learned). They are never interchangeable and a claim must not blur them.

implementation_status.real_runtime_source_of_truth: public/app.js — buildFatelandsMisalignmentPerceptionDirective(), a static (stateless) directive gated on _fatelandsFantasyWorldGate(), wired into the same 3 literary directive-stack call sites and 1 CG call site as buildFatelandsOrdinaryWishMisalignmentDirective and buildFatelandsManifestationLawDirective.
implementation_status.mechanical_check_scope_boundary: This law has NO mechanical validator check anywhere — it is guidance/context only (a capability description an author may or may not need), not a banned/required pattern. Do not build a generic 'perception claim' validator rule from this law without a real, disclosed need.
